Bug demonstration: froster v0.22.0 `archive --recursive` only writes the
froster-archives.json entry when the LAST folder visited by os.walk archived
successfully (Archiver.archive: `if success:` after the walker loop, where
`success` holds only the final iteration's result).

In this captured run the ext4 directory-hash order made os.walk visit
`empty-dir` last. Archiving an empty dir returns None ("contains no files or
symlinks to archive ... skipping" -- see log), so despite all three data
folders uploading and verifying successfully, NO entry was written to
froster-archives.json, and subsequent `froster delete` / `froster restore`
would report "not archived".

os.walk order depends on on-disk directory entry order (ext4 htree hash), so
this is machine-dependent; generate.sh avoids the bug deterministically by
removing empty-dir for the duration of the clean archive run.
